components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Amber action inside dialogs and feature forms.

components.name: Commit Button
components.description: Full-width footer action that commits the current entry.
components.css: .ds-btn-commit { width: 100%; min-height: 52px; padding: 10px 16px; border: 0; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--accent-solid); color: var(--accent-ink); font: 750 13px/1.2 ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif; letter-spacing: -0.01em; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.18s ease, color 0.18s ease; } .ds-btn-commit:hover { background: var(--accent-hover); color: var(--accent-ink); } .ds-btn-commit:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Quiet secondary action beside a primary button.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { min-height: 44px; padding: 10px 16px; border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 999px; background: var(--surface); color: var(--ink); font: 650 13px/1.2 ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.18s ease, border-color 0.18s ease; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: var(--field-hover); border-color: var(--muted); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview:
Cashflow Log looks like the household budget binder that already lives on the kitchen shelf: a graphite desk, matte envelopes, amber index tabs, and stamped states. The surface is precise rather than scrapbooked. Money is the loudest thing on the page, set in tight tabular sans; everything else is a hairline, a label, or a quiet note. The binder metaphor is structural, not decorative: the spread holds a cover, a capture envelope, and the month's page, and the navigation behaves like the tabs that divide them.

The system is dark by default because the primary scene is a family member logging a receipt at the kitchen table after the shops, often in low light; the graphite desk keeps the receipt and the numbers calm. A warm paper theme is available for daylight and for the owner's desktop. Both themes use the same material logic, so a theme change does not change the composition.

The app is an Operate surface: scanning, capture, and correction outrank expression. The amber tab, the stamped reimbursement badge, and the big tabular numerals carry the brand; everything else stays quiet so a receipt can become a verified row without the interface asking for attention.
keyCharacteristics: Graphite desk with matte envelope panels and one warm amber accent.
Binder tabs, stamped states, and tabular numerals as the recurring signature.
Hairlines and spacing carry hierarchy; shadows belong only to floating surfaces.
Phone-first capture with a four-tab binder shell; desktop keeps a sticky rail.
System sans in a tight, confident scale; no serif revival.

rules.name: The One Tab Rule
rules.body: Amber is a state, not a wash. It marks the active tab, the active navigation item, the primary action, and the reimbursement stamp; it never becomes the page background or a decorative gradient.

rules.name: The Stamp Contrast Rule
rules.body: Every amber fill carries Stamp Ink (#1B1207), never white. Every green fill carries the dark income ink; every red fill carries white only where the fill is dark enough.

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Every amount, count, and date column uses font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums and tight tracking; money never wobbles between rows.

rules.name: The No Serif Rule
rules.body: There is no serif in the system. The binder's authority comes from weight, spacing, and the amber tab, not from an editorial face.

rules.name: The Flat-Envelope Rule
rules.body: If a surface is part of the page, it is flat and hairline-bordered. Shadow is reserved for something that can be dismissed, dragged, or floats above the spread.

dos: Do keep the amber tab as the only raised gesture on the capture envelope, at 68×6px.
Do use tabular numerals for every amount, count, and date.
Do clamp long merchant names to two lines and let the amount hold the right edge.
Do keep Camera and Gallery above the sticky commit dock at 390px and 320px.
Do use hairlines, dashed rules, and spacing before reaching for a shadow.
Do flatten history entries into ruled ledger rows with a 1px bottom hairline.
Do theme the browser surface: focus rings, selection, caret, scrollbars, and file inputs come from the same palette.
donts: Don't use gradients, glass, or backdrop blur; the world is matte.
Don't turn every section into a same-size icon/heading/text card, or nest cards inside the history page; the spread is the structure.
Don't use amber for body copy or large background fields; it is a state and an action color.
Don't use a serif or a decorative display face; the system sans is the voice.
Don't hide the month entirely on phones without leaving it available in Overview.
